newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs seen fluctuating on conflicting factors.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs seen fluctuating on conflicting factors.

text.p: Seoul stocks are expected to fluctuate on Friday as sales stemming from financial trouble with the Jinro Group alternate with buying, backed by a high level of liquidity in the market, brokers said.

The planned expansion of the foreign stockholding limit would buoy sentiment, while the news of defects in the high-speed railway now under construction would dampen shares of building companies, they said.
The composite stock index closed 7.66 points lower at 694.76 on Thursday. "Buying will fucus on small-sized shares but blue chips will consolidate further," a LG Securities broker said.
Jinro said on Thursday it has asked for 500 billion won in emergency loans from the Commercial Bank of Korea and SEOULBANK. The group said it urgently needed the money to pay back debts.
Brokers said Jinro's fund shortages deepened as non-banking financial institutions became reluctant to give fresh loans to the group.
Customer deposits were estimated at 3.12 trillion won, up from 3.06 trillion on Monday.
The ceiling for foreign stock ownership is due to be raised to 23 percent on May 2 from the current 20 percent.
